source_version: Capella (continuously deployed, no discrete version number)

relations.subject: sso:realm
relations.evidence:
Choose to turn on or off group mapping.  
Group mapping allows you to assign roles to SSO users based on which teams map to their SSO group.

relations.subject: sso:realm
relations.evidence:
Choose a default team.  
Capella automatically assigns users to the chosen default team when they do not match any team based on their SSO groups.

notable_absence.finding: Prerequisite gate is a linked but generic term - "as a [super administrator](https://support.google.com/a/answer/2405986...#super%5Fadmin)" - functionally equivalent to other providers' 'admin'/'super admin' language, just with an external link where CyberArk/Okta/Ping/OneLogin have none.

cross_component_finding: This is the only provider page with an explicit, separate 'turn the app on for everyone' activation step after the attribute/group configuration is complete (Google Workspace 'User access' > 'On for everyone', noting propagation delay: 'It may take a few minutes for these changes to apply.'). Okta, Ping, and OneLogin fold user/group assignment into the same 'assign users to the application' step with no separate org-wide toggle or propagation-delay caveat; CyberArk and Entra ID likewise have no equivalent wait-time warning. This looks like a genuine platform-level difference (Google's directory propagation lag) rather than a doc inconsistency, but it breaks the otherwise uniform final-step shape of the template.
